scope: RM1 P3-A+B+C review remediation only; no P1 start, migration, seed, reset, Roadmap-state change, or new Journey.
businessUserTask: An operations user selects one owner-confirmed data-node context once, then reads, invites, views detail and revokes users only within that server-owned context.
dexterStageIntent: Close P3 as one atomic delivery with truthful current-byte evidence before any next P, without inventing a new authorization model or broad performance work.

alternatives.reason: It duplicates the already owner-confirmed session context on three feature operations, preserves a client-controlled narrowing surface, and leaves the same-feature consumer removal denominator larger.

It preserves the approved context-switch Journey, makes the selected data node server-owned at every feature endpoint, removes the stale detail/action payload residue, and is smaller than adding a second per-operation scope-selection protocol.

Declare business-verification obligation explicitly, separate dynamic evidence from changed-file receipts, and repair failed-run log/cleanup handling; historical failed-run cause remains UNVERIFIED.
Record concrete server-context, descendant exclusion, peer rejection and leaf-identity assertions in package evidence.
Remove feature-operation scopeRef and derive the selected data-node scope from authenticated session context; test owner-confirmed descendant selection and peer rejection.
Remove scopeRef from every workspace-membership/invitation feature call whose contract no longer accepts it.

changeUnits.failureBehavior: No selected or stale/peer/disabled data node is typed denied; no feature request may select a scope independently of session context.

changeUnits.failureBehavior: A declared business obligation with BLOCKED/FAIL/no current-byte evidence cannot exit PASS; failed remote runs retain sanitized result and independently report cleanup.

closureEvidence.dynamic: Run scoped focused workspace-IAM Testcontainers proof against current source hashes through the repaired managed runner; report business and cleanup separately.
